structured.approach: I followed the DE-02 procedure in the data-engineering-steps skill. I read feat.tasks to find the Data Engineering tasks: TSK-01 and TSK-02, both in ap_pipeline. TSK-01 parses paid_date in transform.py, and TSK-02 adds a pure, no-I/O delays_by_vendor in delays.py. org.permission_table is restricted, so I compared those tasks with it only through the tool view, which says ap_pipeline needs no secrets and is granted none. To confirm the code needs none, I read ingest.py, pipeline.py and schedule.json and searched the checkout case-insensitively for environment-variable, credential and network patterns. Nothing matched. The output lists secret names only: an empty scope for each branch (feature/<story>, dev, main) and no access request. I limited the note on TSK-03 to TSK-08 to what feat.tasks section 1 states, which is the lane each task belongs to. The step was a small lookup, so I did it directly without a helper.

claims.text: The Data Engineering tasks for FEAT-ZD-48600 are TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02), both in the ap_pipeline repository.
feat.tasks section 1 assigns TSK-03 to TSK-08 to the Data Science, Backend, Frontend and Testing Agent lanes.
TSK-02 adds delays_by_vendor in a new src/ap_pipeline/delays.py, a pure function with no I/O.
Feed v3 in production (PQ-6) gates release, not coding. Coding builds on synthetic v3 rows.
No secrets are required or granted for the ap_pipeline repository.
parse_feed parses CSV text with csv.DictReader over io.StringIO. It opens no connection and reads no credential.
pipeline.run chains parse_feed, to_model and quality_report on the CSV text passed to it.
The pipeline schedule is daily at 02:00, Asia/Kolkata.
ap_pipeline uses the Python 3.9 standard library and has the branches main (released), dev (integration) and feature/<story>.
There is no gap between the secrets the DE tasks need and the secrets granted, so no access request was raised.

open_questions: SQ-DE-1 (non-blocking): Will scheduling the pipeline (schedule.json: daily at 02:00, Asia/Kolkata) or sending its status notifications need a scheduler or notification credential? None is needed for TSK-01 or TSK-02, and none is granted.
SQ-DE-2 (non-blocking): Are there deployment environments beyond the main, dev and feature/<story> branches that need their own secret scope? None are named in the inputs.
structured.summary: I rewrote task.secrets_scope for the Data Engineering lane (ap_pipeline). No secrets are needed or granted, and no access request is required. TSK-01 (paid_date parsing) and TSK-02 (the pure delays_by_vendor function) use synthetic data and the standard library only. The permission table's tool view grants no secrets for ap_pipeline. A search of the checkout found no environment-variable, credential or network use. The scope is empty for the feature, dev and main branches. The statement about the other lanes now says only which lane each task belongs to, as feat.tasks section 1 does. Two non-blocking questions remain: credentials for scheduling or notifications, and environments beyond the branches.
